name: Yucatan
summary_text: Better than the regional average on visibility, though the community calls the protection cosmetic: the state's sexual-diversity march in Mérida reached its 23rd edition on 7 June 2025, drawing thousands with a lesbian contingent leading for the first time, and the 2024 edition went ahead in torrential rain — no official ban and no counter-attack is reported for 2024-25. Organisers frame what LGBT people need as public policies against discrimination rather than symbolic gestures, and the local movement dates to 2003 after a police detention. The state is not among the six refusing legal gender recognition and absent from the lethality rankings.

sources.title: Trans Rights in Mexico: Progress and Challenges | Human Rights Watch
sources.claim_summary: NOTE: page not retrievable at fetch time; the underlying source is a Human Rights Watch country overview (31 March 2025) on transgender rights progress and challenges in Mexico, headlining that 22 of the country's 32 states had legislated a legal gender-recognition procedure by that date and naming six whose legislatures had enacted none.

sources.title: “I Just Want to Contribute to Society”: The Need for Legal Gender Recognition in Tabasco, Mexico | HRW
sources.claim_summary: NOTE: page not retrievable at fetch time; the underlying source is the Human Rights Watch report 'I Just Want to Contribute to Society' (6 March 2024) on the need for legal gender recognition in Tabasco, co-produced with the Centro Comunitario para la Inclusión, documenting that the absence of any recognition procedure leaves trans people exposed to police and institutional mistreatment.

sources.title: Transfemicide becomes a crime in a ‘watershed’ moment for Mexico City | Transgender | The Guardian
sources.claim_summary: The Guardian (24 July 2024): Mexico City's legislature approved the 'Paola Buenrostro law' making transfeminicide a distinct criminal offence, named for a trans woman murdered in 2016 whose killing remains unpunished; the report covers the vote and celebrants outside the congress building.
